review_notes: I read the whole target file, `multivariableLaurentTerm` and `multivariableLaurentCoeff` in LaurentSeries/Basic.lean, and `openExtension`, `openExtension_apply` and `openExtension_coe` in FunctionSpace.lean. I also grepped the SeveralComplexVariables directory for other uses of these. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed lemmas would simplify the exact goals here. The `openExtension_apply` finding is the weaker one: it rests on repeated `rw ...; rfl` use, and the right orientation or form for a simp lemma there is a judgment call. I found no loop or competing-rule problems in the simp calls that do appear in the file.

findings.problem: `multivariableLaurentTerm` is an @[expose] def with no simp or unfolding lemmas. Every user unfolds it by name, and the unfolding exposes a raw `(∏ i, z i ^ m i) • c m`. The Kronecker-delta step in this proof is done by hand. It does `by_cases`, `subst`, then `simp only [ite_true, ..., multivariableLaurentTerm, c]` in one branch and `simp [..., multivariableLaurentTerm]` in the other. Line 159 unfolds the term again to prove a vanishing case, and other files do the same: `simp only [multivariableLaurentTerm, hzero k hk, smul_zero]` in Reinhardt/Extension.lean and `simp [multivariableLaurentTerm, hzero]`-style steps in Reinhardt/PartialHull.lean. No file has a named lemma for these routine cases, so each proof depends on the definition's body.
findings.proposed_change: Add small lemmas next to the definition in LaurentSeries/Basic.lean. The first is a definitional unfolding lemma `multivariableLaurentTerm_apply : multivariableLaurentTerm c m z = (∏ i, z i ^ m i) • c m`. The others are @[simp] lemmas for the cases that recur. One covers a zero coefficient, `c m = 0 → multivariableLaurentTerm c m z = 0`. One covers `multivariableLaurentTerm (fun j => if j = k then v else 0) m z = if m = k then multivariableLaurentTerm (fun _ => v) k z else 0`, or an equivalent statement about `Pi.single`. Then lines 205–206 and 213–215 reduce to `simp [hj]` or `simp [hmk]`, with no `subst` or manual unfolding. The same lemmas shorten the unfolding calls in Extension.lean and PartialHull.lean.
findings.benefit: The proofs no longer depend on the body of `multivariableLaurentTerm`. The sparse-coefficient case is handled by one canonical rule, so reordering the definition or changing the summand shape needs a single edit, not edits in several files.

findings.declaration: openExtension_apply (as used in exists_laurentCoeffCLM, exists_laurentTermCLM, exists_laurentProjections)
findings.problem: The only simp lemma for `openExtension` is `openExtension_coe`, which fires only on a subtype-coerced point `↑z`. The commonly needed lemma `openExtension_apply`, for `z ∈ U` given as a hypothesis, is not tagged simp. It is applied by hand with `rw [openExtension_apply U _ hz]` at lines 112, 141, 199 and 220, and also in FunctionSpace.lean, Montel.lean and CartanThullen.lean. The `rw` is often followed by `rfl` (see lines 141–142 and Montel.lean:216) to close a goal that differs only by a subtype wrapper. The explicit `U _ hz` arguments are bookkeeping that a simp lemma with a discharged side condition would avoid. Without such a lemma, the surrounding `simp only [Submodule.coe_sum, ContinuousMap.sum_apply]` at lines 200 and 221 cannot also rewrite `openExtension`. That forces the proof to split into an `rw` step and a simp step.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `openExtension_apply` as @[simp]. Its side condition `z ∈ U` can be discharged from a hypothesis in context when the call is `simp [hz]`. Alternatively, add a companion lemma `openExtension_apply_of_mem` in the same form. Pair it with a simp lemma for `openExtension U (∑ i ∈ s, ↑(f i)) z`, or use `Submodule.coe_sum` and `ContinuousMap.sum_apply` followed by `openExtension_coe`. The `rw ...; simp only ...` pairs at lines 199–200 and 220–221 could then become one `simp [hz]`-style call.
findings.benefit: Users get a single normal form for `openExtension U f z` on points of `U`. The pattern repeated across at least five files becomes one simp call, with no `rfl` fix-up and no explicit `U _ hz` arguments.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem openExtension_apply (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens E)
    (f : C(U, F)) {z : E} (hz : z ∈ U) : openExtension U f z = f ⟨z, hz⟩
(hA n).congr V.isOpen (fun z hz => by rw [openExtension_apply V _ hz]; rfl)
